editorial:
Imagine you just had a baby and you are totally exhausted. That is exactly where Caitlin and Miguel are when they meet Polly. She seems like the perfect nanny, always smiling and knowing exactly how to calm the baby down. You will feel that same sense of relief they do at first, but it does not last long. The vibe shifts quickly from a cozy home movie to a tense game of cat and mouse. You can feel the stress building up as Polly starts moving into their lives in ways that feel wrong, making you wonder why she is really there.

The acting is top-notch, especially the actress playing Polly, who can go from sweet to scary in a second. The plot moves fast and keeps you guessing with some solid twists that you will not see coming. While some parts feel a bit like other nanny movies, the tension is real.
endingExplained: In the end, you find out Polly is actually related to the family and wants to steal the baby to replace a child she lost years ago. She tries to frame Caitlin as an unfit mother to get legal control of the infant. After a scary fight in the house, Miguel and Caitlin manage to outsmart her. Polly is finally caught by the police, and the couple recovers their baby, finally safe in their own home.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers and stories about secrets.
similarMovies: The Hand That Rocks the Cradle
